answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake: before trading, an agent publishes a public cipher key tied to a locked deposit, and every deal is signed with it. Reputation then accumulates at one vertex — the agent's persistent identity node — instead of spreading across disposable accounts. New identities start on the ridge of trust with near-zero weight and must earn standing through attested work, so spawning a hundred fake agents costs a hundred deposits and a hundred histories, while a swarm cannot inherit the standing of the vertex it copies.
